fields.h1: Build Lead Generation Automation That Captures Each Lead Once
fields.hero_description: Build lead generation automation that saves every chat, form, and webinar lead with its source in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Behind Every Lead Form
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the capture, the checks, and the hand-off to sales as one app, from a description of how leads reach you today.
fields.feature_1:
One lead table for every source

Chat, the website form, the quote form, and webinar signups all write to the same lead table. Every row carries the same fields, so a lead reads the same whatever its source.
fields.feature_2:
The source and campaign on each lead

The app saves where each lead came from: the page, the form, and the UTM campaign in the link. Reports then count leads by that source without anyone tagging a row by hand.
fields.feature_3:
A duplicate check before a lead is created

Before it writes a new lead, the app looks up the email address. A match adds the new signup to the existing record, and its history keeps every way that person came in.
fields.feature_4:
Leads written to your CRM through its API

The app writes each lead to HubSpot or any CRM with an API and reads back the owner and stage. Sales keeps working where it already works, with the source fields filled in.
fields.feature_5:
A message when a lead needs a person

Pick the leads that should reach someone right away, such as demo requests. The app sends that person a Slack message or an email with the answers and a link to the record.
fields.feature_6:
The lead app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of your lead generation app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Anyone on your team can read how leads are matched and stored, and change it.

plan.angle: The live SERP for lead generation automation is software roundups, agency explainers and video tutorials that list tools in general terms. This page shows the capture end of the funnel as a working app: a pricing-page chat that writes a lead, a quote form that checks the service area first, a duplicate check that adds a second signup to the existing record, and a Monday digest that counts leads by source. It stays on getting leads in clean and attributed, and leaves scoring, routing and nurture emails to the lead scoring automation, lead routing automation and lead nurturing workflow pages. The FAQ covers lead gen vs demand gen, chat qualification, capture fields, duplicates and source tracking as operator advice.
tab_stories: Corlander Scheduling runs a 4-question chat on its pricing page: Imogen Faulkes, clinic director at Bramcote Physio, answers all 4 one screen at a time, and the app writes her lead to HubSpot with every answer and the page she chatted on.

Sorrelton Roofing takes quote requests from its website form and serves 14 zip codes: a request from Ottavine Kestermann in a zip code outside them gets a reply email naming the area the company covers, and it is saved as out of area instead of reaching the estimator.

Mirefield Analytics already has Rhea Vandermolen from a pricing guide download 3 weeks ago; when she registers for the Thursday webinar with the same email, the app adds the webinar to her record, so she stays one lead with 2 sources.

Wendling Fleet Parts gets a Slack digest every Monday at 9 am: 212 leads last week, 71 from the website form, 58 from paid search, 46 from webinars and 37 from dealer referrals, with paid search flagged for falling from 90.
